messages:
incident-bot: [31mALERT[0m prod: high 5xx ratio on /v1/generate >8% for 5m. PagerDuty PD-2048 notified. Observability: Datadog shows metric ingestion lag and gaps for the last ~10m.

jon: grabbing oncall. seeing spike in upstream 502/504 in nginx logs. datadog dashboards look truncated around 1750101180. Priya, can you confirm traces/alerts?

priya: dd UI shows partial traces missing and some dashboards show "No data" tiles. I pinged Datadog support (ticket DD-7012). their initial response: "Investigating ingestion delays in US/EU regions."

sam: if Datadog is blind, switch to Prometheus and our s3-access-log parser for immediate visibility. Enabled extra app-level debug logs to s3.

emily: customers are already opening tickets: CS-1022 and CS-1023 reporting timeouts. CS team sent quick acknowledgement via cs-bot.

jon: immediate mitigation: 1) suppress Datadog-derived alerts to avoid alert storm, 2) flip alerting to Prometheus rules, 3) enable local log retention and start a live stream to S3. implementing now.

priya: applied suppression to "api-5xx-alert" in Datadog and created equivalent PromAlert rule in AlertManager. Command used:
```
kubectl apply -f prometheus/alerts/api-5xx-fallback.yaml
```

sam: Prometheus query to use for postmortem and live dashboards:
```
rate(http_requests_total{job="api",status=~"5.."}[1m])
```

jon: also increasing proxy read_timeout 10s->20s to reduce client timeouts while upstream stabilizes. doing a canary of 5% first.

emily: CS updated impacted customers with the templated message. they're asking for ETA and timeline. Logged requests from affected accounts for postmortem.

monitoring-bot: Datadog status update: "Partial ingestion delays affecting metrics and traces. Investigating." https://status.datadoghq.com/incidents/ef56

priya: Datadog chat notes: they confirm backlog causing up to 15m delay in metric ingestion. No data loss reported. They requested our time window and example metric names.

sam: traffic canary at 1750101280 shows 5xx rate on canary hosts decreased by ~50% vs baseline. Prometheus dashboards reflect the change.

jon: switching 25% traffic to region-b as a safety step; route changes applied via traffic-router. Monitor Prometheus and jaeger fallback.

emily: CS opened a private slack channel with impacted enterprise customers and posted interim updates. They're asking for a post-incident timeline and RCA.

priya: collecting evidence for postmortem: Prometheus graphs, nginx logs, s3 logs, and jaeger traces where available. Note: Datadog window of reduced visibility: 1750101120 -> 1750101320. Marking that in the timeline.

jon: oncall handoff plan: I'll keep incident leadership for the next 20m then hand to priya for post-incident tasks. Priya, please continue Datadog escalation if they don't publish a final timeline.

priya: acknowledged. I've asked Datadog for a post-incident summary and log-level timeline. Also requested priority escalation due to customer impact.

monitoring-bot: PD-2048 status updated to "mitigated" at 1750101375. Assignee: jon -> priya.

sam: prepping postmortem doc and will include a section on "observability blindness" and fallback procedures we executed (Prometheus alerts, s3 logs, jaeger). Will include the commands and snippets used.

emily: support follow-up: sending customers a timeline and action items; CS will request credits for affected accounts per policy.

priya: final status: error rates back to baseline after traffic shifts and proxy change. Datadog ingestion catching up ~1750101380-1750101390. Waiting on Datadog confirmation.

incident-bot: INCIDENT PD-2048 closed at 1750101399. Summary: transient upstream errors combined with Datadog ingestion delays created visibility blind spots. Mitigations: alert failover to Prometheus, increased proxy timeouts, traffic shift to region-b, additional log retention. Postmortem tracked in internal doc: https://docs.internal/redwood/incidents/PD-2048
